rows.practice: analyses the central texts of religious traditions and secondary scholarship with historical, textual, anthropological and theological methods and gathers primary material from texts or fieldwork
rows.knowledge: the key sources of the traditions studied and how they have been read over time, lived religious practice and material culture together with non-religion, atheism and secular culture
rows.identity: a student of religion who is critically aware of their own commitments and prejudices and meets the convictions of others with empathy and integrity

rows.practice: brings religious ideas into debate with law, the sciences and public life, argues a position while representing rival views fairly and practises with critical insight in unpredictable ministerial settings
rows.knowledge: how religion forms personal and shared identity for good and harm, how religious identities are renegotiated and hybrid and what religions add to public debate on justice and truth
rows.identity: a scholar of religion who listens for marginalised voices in communities and in the field itself and weighs the effects of strong conviction in religious and secular groups alike

rows.practice: conducts original research on religion with suitable methods, analyses primary sources and scholarship with sophistication and reaches independent conclusions from material it has located itself
rows.knowledge: the complexity of religious subject matter, which sources suit a given inquiry and the ethical questions and codes of practice that research on religion raises
rows.identity: a self-directing researcher who examines the paradigms they use so as to reduce the marginalisation and exclusion those paradigms carry and keeps research ethics in view

digest.definition: A field that studies religion and religions critically and globally, including non-religion, atheism and the secular, so that people can understand and act in a world religion shapes
distinctiveFeatures: A field that studies religion and religions critically and globally, including non-religion, atheism and the secular, so that people can understand and act in a world religion shapes

Its identity is itself debated: one internally varied discipline, or theology and religious studies as two linked disciplines; insider and outsider stances and views on truth claims cut across the debate
It is taught in secular providers open to any belief and in providers with a religious stance, some training for ministry or chaplaincy, under many course titles
Courses are built for breadth (several traditions) or depth (one tradition, often with its languages) or a mix
It works through many approaches, textual, historical, social scientific, philosophical, theological, feminist, postcolonial and others, and draws on and feeds many neighbouring subjects
It engages directly with living religion through study visits, fieldwork, placements and partnership with religious communities, which calls for respect and handles unsettling critique
It can change students personally, but a student's spiritual development and religious outlook are not award criteria

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: belonging for students of every belief and background; a declared religious stance that students may challenge; a decolonising approach to content, pedagogy and assessment; critical awareness of the field's own role in categorising religions; religion as a protected characteristic; inclusion and identity questions in every course (D1, 1.15, 1.22 to 1.25, 2.11, 3.5, A3)

entry without school religious studies; part-time, online and blended modes; accessible language materials; design for disabled students and specific learning differences; accessible fieldwork, placements and discussion, including for autistic and socially anxious students (D1, 2.4 to 2.11, 3.12, 3.23)

where social, economic, cultural and environmental concerns meet religion and spirituality; the eight UNESCO competencies each given a religious angle; a stated link to the decolonising approach; sustainability questions in every course and in public debate (D1, 1.14, 1.26 to 1.29, 3.5, 4.6)

named with employability as one theme; graduates valued for cross-disciplinary skill and empathy; placements, workplace modules, community challenges and practitioner teaching; innovation in religious roles; review with employability in view (D1, 1.17 to 1.21, 1.30 to 1.33, 2.21)

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject
statements.about: empathetic engagement with familiar and unfamiliar views
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will have the knowledge, understanding and practical skill to engage with empathy with views both familiar and strange to them, which a diverse society needs.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to engage empathetically with familiar and unfamiliar viewpoints, a skill set the issuer ties to employability in a diverse society.

forBeneficiary.text: You will gain the knowledge and practical skill to engage with empathy with views you know and views new to you, which matters in a diverse society.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: institutions or courses with a religious identity or stance
statements.about: declaring and opening to challenge a religious stance
statements.paraphrase: Where an institution or course holds a particular religious identity or stance, it will tell all students so, and students will be able to examine, question and challenge it and weigh other perspectives.

forPractitioner.text: If your institution or course has a religious identity or stance, make it clear to every student, and build in real chances for students to examine, question and challenge it and to explore alternatives.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the institution or course; the student meets its effect (being told and free to challenge), not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: all courses in the field
statements.about: designing for disabled students and learning differences
statements.paraphrase: Every course in the field will be designed with the needs of disabled students and students with specific learning differences in mind.

forPractitioner.text: Design every course with disabled students and students with specific learning differences in mind from the start: varied formats, varied forms of engagement and assessment and accessible materials.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: courses using discussion and interpersonal activities
statements.about: accessible discussion for autistic and socially anxious students
statements.paraphrase: Where courses rely on discussion and other interpersonal work, these will be run with attention to the needs of autistic students and those with social anxiety.

forPractitioner.text: Run discussion and other interpersonal activities with the needs of autistic students and students with social anxiety in mind.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on how teaching is delivered; not a standard for the student

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: students progressing through an honours course
statements.about: writing and research skills; the major project
statements.paraphrase: Progression will include gaining academic writing and research skills so that students learn and research more and more independently; single honours courses will generally offer a major project or dissertation to secure that independence.

forPractitioner.text: Plan progression so that students build academic writing and research skills towards independence; in single honours, generally offer a major project or dissertation as one route to it.

forBeneficiary.text: As you progress you will build academic writing and research skills and become a more independent learner and researcher, usually with a major project or dissertation in a single honours course.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: joint honours undergraduates
statements.about: skills reached on joint honours courses
statements.paraphrase: Joint honours students will reach part of the subject-specific and generic skills, adding further skills from the other subjects in their course.

forPractitioner.text: On joint honours, expect students to reach elements of this subject's specific and generic skills, complemented by skills from the partner subject.

forBeneficiary.text: On a joint honours course you will gain some of this subject's specific and general skills and add others from your other subject.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: courses engaging with religious communities
statements.about: respectful engagement with religious communities
statements.paraphrase: Courses will always engage with religious communities respectfully.

forPractitioner.text: Conduct every engagement between the course and religious communities respectfully, even where critical analysis unsettles convictions.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on how courses deal with communities; students take part, but the standard is the course's

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: degree-awarding bodies reviewing courses in the field
statements.about: external reference points and employability in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Awarding bodies will use external reference points, this statement among them, to keep provision in line with sector norms, and periodic review in the field will consider employability, for example fit with initial teacher training standards.

forPractitioner.text: In periodic review, use external reference points, this statement included, to check alignment with sector norms, and address employability, for example alignment with initial teacher training standards.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the awarding body's review process

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Theology and Religious Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: higher education providers in periodic review
statements.about: external reviewers in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Providers will involve external reviewers in periodic review to get an outside view of planned changes and to check that threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Include external reviewers in periodic review to test proposed changes and to confirm threshold standards are met and content fits the subject.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider's review process

statements.appliesTo: all courses in the field
statements.about: sustainability, inclusion and identity in every course
statements.paraphrase: Whatever mix of content a course chooses, it is essential that every course examines its subject matter in the light of sustainability and of inclusion and identity (gender, race, class, sexuality, postcoloniality).

forPractitioner.text: Whatever content mix you choose, make sure the subject matter is examined in relation to sustainability and to inclusion and identity, including gender, race, class, sexuality and postcoloniality.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on course content; the student meets it through what is taught

statements.appliesTo: formative assessment in courses in the field

statements.paraphrase: Formative tasks will give students chances to build the skills and understanding their summative work needs, and to get feedback that helps them develop.

forPractitioner.text: Design formative tasks so that they build the skills and understanding summative tasks need, with feedback that supports that growth.

statements.about: religions and worldviews, general and particular
statements.paraphrase: Will show that they understand and engage critically with religion and worldviews in general, with specific religious traditions and their communities and institutions or with both.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show understanding of, and critical engagement with, religions and worldviews broadly, particular traditions with their communities and institutions or both.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will show that you understand, and can think critically about, religion and worldviews as a whole, specific traditions and their communities or both.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: non-religion, atheism and the secular
statements.paraphrase: Will show understanding of, and critical engagement with, non-religion and atheism and with how religions relate to secular culture.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand and critically engage with non-religion, atheism and the relations between religions and the secular.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will understand, and think critically about, non-belief and atheism and how religion and secular society relate.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: lived religion and its links to wider society
statements.paraphrase: Will show understanding of, and critical engagement with, a selection of the lived aspects of the traditions studied (practice, belief, ethics, text, material culture, art, history and more) and how these connect with wider social and cultural patterns.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically understand some of the practical, material, textual and historical dimensions of the traditions they studied and relate them to wider social and cultural structures.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will understand and think critically about some of the ways the traditions you study are lived (practices, beliefs, texts, objects, art, history) and how they connect with the wider society around them.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: changing religious identities and hybridity
statements.paraphrase: Will show a sophisticated grasp of how religious identities and cultures are continually renegotiated, change, meet and clash, and of hybrid and multiple belonging.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand in a sophisticated way the ongoing renegotiation of religious identities and cultures, including hybridity and multiple belonging.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will have a sophisticated grasp of how religious identities keep shifting, meet and clash, and how people can belong to more than one tradition.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: key sources and how they have been read
statements.paraphrase: Will show understanding of, and critical engagement with, the central sources of the traditions or worldviews studied and how they have been interpreted across periods and settings.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically understand the key sources of the religions or worldviews studied and their interpretation across history and social or geographical settings.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will understand and think critically about the main sources of the traditions you study and how people have read them in different times and places.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: claims about the transcendent, the world, ethics and flourishing
statements.paraphrase: Will show understanding of, and critical engagement with, the beliefs and arguments circulating in particular religious settings about transcendent reality, the divine, the world, ethics and human flourishing.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically understand the beliefs and arguments about the divine or transcendent, the world, ethics and flourishing current in specified religious contexts.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will understand and think critically about what particular religious groups believe and argue about God or the divine, the world, ethics and living well.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: themes, debates and methods of the field
statements.paraphrase: Will show understanding of, and critical engagement with, a range of the themes, debates and methods that make up theology and religious studies.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically understand a range of the field's themes, debates and methods.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will understand and think critically about a range of the topics, debates and methods in the study of theology and religion.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: applying the field to interdisciplinary discussion
statements.paraphrase: Will bring the field's ideas, themes and debates to bear, appropriately, on discussions shared with other disciplines in the humanities, social sciences, law or the sciences.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will apply the insights and debates of the field appropriately to interdisciplinary conversations, for example with law, the social sciences or the sciences.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to use ideas and debates from theology and religious studies sensibly in conversations with other subjects, such as law, social science or medicine.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Knowledge and understanding

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: religion's contributions to public debate
statements.paraphrase: Will show awareness of, and assess critically, what religions contribute to public debate on matters such as justice, identity, diversity, inclusion, poverty, race, sustainability and truth.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be aware of and critically assess religious contributions to public debate on topics such as diversity, inclusion, justice, poverty, race and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be aware of how religious voices take part in public debates (on justice, identity, race, poverty, sustainability and more) and be able to assess them critically.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Subject-specific and intellectual skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: intellectual flexibility across methods of study
statements.paraphrase: Will show flexibility of mind by working with a variety of methods of study, from anthropological, historical and textual to feminist, postcolonial, queer, theological and others.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show intellectual flexibility by practising varied methods of study (for example exegetical, empirical, feminist, postcolonial, systematic or theological).

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will show flexible thinking by using several different methods to study religion, such as historical, textual, social scientific, feminist or theological approaches.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Subject-specific and intellectual skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: evaluating primary and secondary sources
statements.paraphrase: Will judge and analyse critically many original and secondary sources by varied authors and from varied settings, from the field and, where relevant, from related subjects.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically evaluate and analyse a wide range of primary and secondary material from diverse authors and contexts, within and beyond the field.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to judge and analyse critically a wide range of original and secondary sources by varied authors, including some from related subjects.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Subject-specific and intellectual skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: how religion shapes identity and motivation
statements.paraphrase: Will show a sophisticated grasp of how religion forms personal and shared identities and motives, of the good and harm this can do and of why such identities matter.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show sophisticated understanding of how religion shapes personal and communal identity and motivation for good and ill and how much it matters.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will show a sophisticated understanding of how religion shapes who people are and what drives them for better and worse and why that matters.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Subject-specific and intellectual skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: conviction and certainty and their effects
statements.paraphrase: Will show a sensitive awareness of strong conviction and claimed certainty found in religious and non-religious groups and institutions, with their good and bad effects.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show sensitive awareness of conviction and claims to certainty in religious and non-religious settings, and their positive and negative effects.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will show a sensitive awareness of strong conviction and certainty, in religious and non-religious groups alike, and of the good and harm they can do.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Subject-specific and intellectual skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: marginalised voices and the causes of marginalisation
statements.paraphrase: Will show awareness of, and sensitivity to, voices pushed to the margins in religious communities, in public talk about religion and in the field itself, and awareness of what causes this.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show awareness of and sensitivity to marginalised voices in communities, public discourse and the discipline, and understand where marginalisation comes from.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will notice and respond with care to voices that get pushed aside, in religious groups, in public debate and in this subject itself, and understand why that happens.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Subject-specific and intellectual skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: critically informed practice in vocational courses
statements.paraphrase: On professional, vocational and ministerial courses, will show they can practise with sophistication, creativity and critical insight in complex settings that cannot be predicted.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates of professional, vocational and ministerial courses will show they can practise in a sophisticated, creative and critically informed way in complex, unpredictable contexts.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, if your course is professional, vocational or ministerial, you will show you can practise thoughtfully, creatively and critically in complex and unpredictable situations.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: communicating to an audience in varied forms
statements.paraphrase: Will convey information, ideas, arguments and theories to a chosen audience in several forms, spoken, visual and written, including a well organised dissertation or extended project.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will communicate ideas and arguments to a defined audience orally, visually and in writing of varied lengths, including a clearly organised dissertation or extended project.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to get ideas and arguments across to a particular audience by speaking, visuals and writing, including a long, well organised project or dissertation.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: independent thought and critical self-awareness
statements.paraphrase: Will think independently and be critically aware of their own outlooks, commitments and prejudices.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show independent thought and critical self-awareness of their own outlooks, commitments and biases.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will think for yourself and be critically aware of your own views, commitments and biases.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: arguing a view while treating others fairly
statements.paraphrase: Will argue for their own position while fairly acknowledging, representing and engaging with the positions of others.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will argue their own views while fairly acknowledging, representing and engaging with others' views.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to argue for your own view while setting out other people's views fairly and responding to them.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: empathetic, critical engagement with others
statements.paraphrase: Will engage with the convictions and conduct of others with empathy and integrity while reflecting critically.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will engage with other people's convictions and behaviour empathetically, with integrity and critical reflection.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will engage with what other people believe and do with empathy and integrity, while still thinking critically.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: teamwork
statements.paraphrase: Will work with others in a team or group so that each member's strengths are used well.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will work collaboratively in a team or group, making good use of each member's talents.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to work in a group so that everyone's strengths are put to good use.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: self-directed study and reflection on learning
statements.paraphrase: Will study independently or in a self-directed way while managing their time, and reflect on what they do well and less well as learners.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will undertake self-directed study, manage their time and reflect on their own strengths and weaknesses as learners.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to organise your own study and time and reflect on what you do well and less well as a learner.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: gathering and analysing primary material
statements.paraphrase: Will find, collect and analyse primary data and source material, through work on texts or in the field.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will identify, gather and analyse primary data and sources, whether textual or from fieldwork.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will be able to find, collect and analyse original material yourself, from texts or from fieldwork.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: using resources to find material and compile bibliographies
statements.paraphrase: Will use the full range of resources well to locate suitable material, build bibliographies, inform research and strengthen presentations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will use the whole range of resources well to find material, compile bibliographies, inform research and improve presentations.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will use the whole range of resources to find good material, build reference lists, support your research and improve your presentations.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in the subject, at the threshold
statements.about: technology for sources, research and presentation
statements.paraphrase: Will use technology and computing skills suitably to find material and data, support research and improve presentations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will use technology and computer skills appropriately to locate sources and data, support research and enhance presentations.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for an honours award, you will use digital tools and computer skills sensibly to find material and data, support your research and improve your presentations.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A3 Intended entrants

statements.appliesTo: applicants for master's degrees in the field
statements.about: entry above the honours threshold
statements.paraphrase: The honours standards show the kind of knowledge and skill a master's will need, but applicants will need to have shown them above the threshold.

forPractitioner.text: When admitting to a master's, look for evidence of the honours outcomes at a level above the threshold, not merely at it.

forBeneficiary.text: To start a master's in this field you will need to have shown the undergraduate knowledge and skills at more than the minimum level.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A3 Intended entrants

statements.appliesTo: master's degrees in the field
statements.about: open access to master's study
statements.paraphrase: As a rule, master's degrees in the field should be open to every student, whatever their religious belief, gender, race, sexuality or disability.

forPractitioner.text: Keep master's admission open to all, regardless of religious belief, gender, race, sexuality or disability, save where A3 allows a genuine occupational requirement.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in admissions

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A3 Intended entrants

statements.appliesTo: master's courses training for work in particular religious bodies
statements.about: transparency and freedom to challenge in confessional training
statements.paraphrase: Where affiliation is a genuine requirement, the course will tell all applicants its nature, and students will still be able to examine, question and challenge the religious body's stance and consider alternatives.

forPractitioner.text: Where religious affiliation is a genuine occupational requirement, make the course's nature clear to every applicant and keep room for students to question and challenge the sponsoring body's stance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A4 Teaching and learning

statements.appliesTo: master's students in the field
statements.about: considering the ethics of study and research
statements.paraphrase: Master's students are expected to show that they have thought about the ethical questions their study, and above all their research, raises.

forPractitioner.text: Expect master's students to show they have considered the ethics of their study and especially of their research, with reference to relevant standards such as the subject association's Framework of Professional Practice.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's you will be expected to show that you have thought through the ethical questions your study, and especially your research, raises.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: independence and self-direction in learning
statements.paraphrase: Has shown a large measure of independence and self-direction, owning their learning and locating much of their own material.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have shown strong independence and self-direction, taking charge of their learning and sourcing much of their own material.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, a high level of independence: you take charge of your own learning and find much of your own material.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: research methods and skills
statements.paraphrase: Has shown knowledge of suitable research methods and put suitable research skills to use.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have shown they know fitting research methods and can apply the research skills those methods need.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, that you know which research methods suit a question and can use the skills they need.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: sophisticated analysis of sources
statements.paraphrase: Has analysed relevant primary sources and secondary scholarship in a sophisticated way.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have analysed relevant primary sources and secondary literature with sophistication.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, a sophisticated analysis of original sources and of what scholars have written about them.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: skills for original research and independent conclusions
statements.paraphrase: Has shown the skills to produce original research (below doctoral originality), standing back from and critically evaluating their material and reaching their own conclusions.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have shown they can produce original research short of doctoral originality, keep critical distance from their sources and reach independent conclusions.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, that you can produce original research of your own (not yet doctoral in its originality), step back from your sources, judge them critically and reach your own conclusions.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: complexity of the subject and range of sources
statements.paraphrase: Has shown critical awareness of how complex the subject matter is and of which sources fit their work.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have shown critical awareness of the subject's complexity and of the range of sources suited to their work.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, that you are critically aware of how complex your subject is and which kinds of source suit your work.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: reflecting on paradigms to reduce marginalisation
statements.paraphrase: Has reflected critically on the frameworks and perspectives they use, aiming to lessen the marginalisation and exclusion those frameworks carry.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have reflected critically on their own paradigms and perspectives, aiming to reduce the marginalisation and exclusion built into them.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, critical reflection on the frameworks you use, so that you can lessen the ways they push some people or views aside.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: research ethics and codes of practice
statements.paraphrase: Has understood the ethical questions their research raises and kept to the relevant codes of practice.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have understood the ethics of their own research and complied with relevant codes of practice.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, that you understand the ethical questions your research raises and follow the codes of practice that apply.

headingPath: Appendix A: Taught master's degrees; A6 Benchmark standards

statements.appliesTo: taught master's graduates in the subject
statements.about: online resources and tools
statements.paraphrase: Has shown they can judge critically and use online resources and tools for study and research.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates have shown they can critically evaluate and use online resources and tools for study and research.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will typically show, among other things, that you can judge critically and use online resources and tools for study and research.
